static-gk: What is the capital of Australia?
Canberra is Australia's capital. Sydney is the largest city.
'Wings of Fire' is the autobiography of which person?
Wings of Fire (1999) is the autobiography of Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam, written with Arun Tiwari.
National Sports Day in India is celebrated on which date?
National Sports Day is on 29 August, the birth anniversary of hockey player Major Dhyan Chand.
What is the currency of Japan?
Japan's currency is the yen. The yuan is China's and the won is Korea's.
Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean.
Who wrote India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
Jana Gana Mana was written by Rabindranath Tagore. Bankim Chandra wrote the national song, Vande Mataram.
Where is the headquarters of the United Nations?
The UN headquarters is in New York City, USA.
The Bharat Ratna is India's highest award in which category?
The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award.
Which country is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
Japan is called the Land of the Rising Sun; its name in Japanese means 'origin of the sun'.
International Day of Yoga is observed on which date?
The UN declared 21 June as International Day of Yoga; it was first observed in 2015.
general-science: What is the chemical symbol of sodium?
Sodium's symbol is Na, from its Latin name natrium.
Which part of the cell is called its 'powerhouse'?
Mitochondria release energy from food through cellular respiration.
What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
Light travels at about 3 × 10^8 metres per second (about 3 lakh km per second) in a vacuum.
Which vitamin is made in the human skin when it is exposed to sunlight?
Sunlight (UV-B rays) helps the skin make vitamin D.
Which gas makes up most of the Earth's atmosphere?
Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the air; oxygen is about 21%.
What is the pH of pure water at 25 °C?
Pure water is neutral, with a pH of 7 at 25 °C.
Which blood components help the blood to clot?
Platelets gather at a wound and help form a clot.
What is the SI unit of force?
Force is measured in newtons (N). Joule is the unit of energy and watt of power.
Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
Diamond, a form of carbon, is the hardest natural substance.
Insulin is produced by which organ?
Insulin is made by the beta cells of the pancreas and controls blood sugar.
indian-history: In which year was the Battle of Plassey fought?
The Battle of Plassey (1757) was won by the British East India Company under Robert Clive against Siraj-ud-Daulah.
Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire around 321 BCE, with the help of Chanakya.
In which year did the Jallianwala Bagh massacre take place?
The massacre took place in Amritsar on 13 April 1919.
In which year did Mahatma Gandhi begin the Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha)?
The Dandi March began on 12 March 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram.
In which year was the Indian National Congress founded?
The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885; its first session was held in Bombay.
Who started the construction of the Qutub Minar?
Qutb-ud-din Aibak began the Qutub Minar; Iltutmish and later rulers completed and repaired it.
In which year was the Quit India Movement launched?
The Quit India Movement was launched on 8 August 1942.
Who was the first Indian Governor-General of independent India?
C. Rajagopalachari was the first and only Indian Governor-General (1948–1950). Lord Mountbatten was the first Governor-General of independent India.
Which Harappan site is famous for its dockyard?
Lothal in Gujarat had a dockyard, showing that Harappans traded by sea.
Who gave the slogan 'Do or Die'?
Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' during the Quit India Movement in 1942.
geography: Which is the longest river in India?
The Ganga is the longest river flowing within India, at about 2,525 km.
Which is the highest mountain peak in the world?
Mount Everest, on the Nepal–China border, is about 8,849 m high.
The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which of these states?
The Tropic of Cancer passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram. It does not pass through Odisha.
Which is the largest state of India by area?
Rajasthan is India's largest state by area.
The Palk Strait separates India from which country?
The Palk Strait lies between Tamil Nadu and northern Sri Lanka.
Which is the largest planet in our solar system?
Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
Which line forms the boundary between India and Pakistan?
The Radcliffe Line was drawn in 1947. The McMahon Line relates to China and the Durand Line separates Pakistan and Afghanistan.
Black soil is best suited for growing which crop?
Black (regur) soil holds moisture well and is ideal for cotton, so it is also called black cotton soil.
Australia is the smallest continent by area.
Chilika Lake is located in which state?
Chilika, in Odisha, is the largest brackish-water lagoon in India.
indian-polity: Which article of the Indian Constitution abolishes untouchability?
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and makes its practice in any form an offence.
On which date was the Constitution of India adopted by the Constituent Assembly?
It was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950.
Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'?
Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.
What is the minimum age to be elected President of India?
Article 58 sets the minimum age for the President at 35 years.
What is the normal term of the Lok Sabha?
The Lok Sabha's normal term is five years unless dissolved earlier.
Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which amendment?
The 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties in Part IV-A (Article 51A).
Which article provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies?
Article 32 lets citizens approach the Supreme Court to enforce Fundamental Rights. Dr Ambedkar called it the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.
Who appoints the Chief Justice of India?
The President appoints the Chief Justice of India under Article 124.
Why is the Rajya Sabha called a permanent house?
Its members are nominated for life
The Rajya Sabha is never dissolved; about one-third of its members retire every two years.
How many Fundamental Rights does the Indian Constitution currently provide?
There are six. The Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment (1978).
indian-economy: In which year was the Reserve Bank of India established?
The RBI was set up on 1 April 1935 and nationalised in 1949.
From which date was GST implemented in India?
Goods and Services Tax came into force on 1 July 2017.
NITI Aayog replaced which body in 2015?
NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission on 1 January 2015.
Which ministry prepares the Union Budget?
The Union Budget is prepared by the Ministry of Finance and presented by the Finance Minister.
The rate at which banks lend to customers
The rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks
The rate banks pay on savings accounts
The tax rate on bank profits
Repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends short-term money to commercial banks against securities.
Where is the headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India?
The RBI's central office is in Mumbai.
Which organisation releases India's official GDP estimates?
GDP estimates are released by the National Statistics Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.
The ₹1 currency note is issued by whom?
Ministry of Finance, Government of India
The ₹1 note is issued by the Ministry of Finance and signed by the Finance Secretary; other notes are issued by the RBI.
How many days of wage employment per year does MGNREGA guarantee to a rural household?
MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment a year to every rural household that asks for work.
Who is known as the 'Father of the Green Revolution in India'?
Agricultural scientist M. S. Swaminathan led the Green Revolution in India. Verghese Kurien is linked with the White Revolution (milk).
current-affairs: In which year did Chandrayaan-3 land near the Moon's south pole?
Chandrayaan-3's lander Vikram touched down on 23 August 2023, making India the first country to land near the lunar south pole.
In which year did India host the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi?
India held the G20 presidency in 2023 and hosted the summit in New Delhi in September 2023.
What is the name of India's first space mission to study the Sun, launched in 2023?
Aditya-L1 was launched by ISRO on 2 September 2023 and studies the Sun from the L1 point.
In which year was India's new Parliament building inaugurated?
The new Parliament building in New Delhi was inaugurated on 28 May 2023.
Which city hosted the 2024 Summer Olympic Games?
Paris hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics. Los Angeles will host in 2028.
Which country hosted the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023?
India hosted the 2023 ICC Men's Cricket World Cup; Australia won the final in Ahmedabad.
The Women's Reservation Act, 2023 reserves what share of seats in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies for women?
The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, 2023 reserves one-third of seats for women.
Which team won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024?
India beat South Africa in the final in Barbados on 29 June 2024.
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, which came into force in July 2024, replaced which law?
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita replaced the Indian Penal Code (1860) from 1 July 2024.
Through which mission did Indian astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla travel to the International Space Station in 2025?
Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS on Axiom Mission 4 (Ax-4) in June 2025.
environment: The ozone layer protects the Earth from which radiation?
The ozone layer in the stratosphere absorbs most of the Sun's harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation.
Which is the main greenhouse gas released by burning fossil fuels?
Burning coal, oil and gas releases carbon dioxide, the main human-made greenhouse gas.
The Kyoto Protocol is related to which issue?
The Kyoto Protocol (1997) set targets to cut greenhouse gas emissions. The Montreal Protocol deals with the ozone layer.
In which year was Project Tiger launched in India?
Project Tiger was launched on 1 April 1973 to protect tigers and their habitats.
World Environment Day is observed on which date?
World Environment Day is on 5 June. Earth Day is on 22 April.
The Chipko Movement was mainly about what?
In the Chipko Movement (1970s, in present-day Uttarakhand), villagers hugged trees to stop them being cut.
Which is the largest mangrove forest in the world?
The Sundarbans, shared by India and Bangladesh, is the world's largest mangrove forest.
Which chemicals are mainly responsible for depleting the ozone layer?
CFCs, once used in fridges and sprays, release chlorine that destroys ozone.
Silent Valley National Park is in which state?
Silent Valley National Park is in Kerala's Palakkad district, in the Western Ghats.
Which region of India is a global biodiversity hotspot?
The Western Ghats (with Sri Lanka) is one of the world's biodiversity hotspots. India's others are the Himalaya, Indo-Burma and Sundaland.
